Troops of the Nigerian Army have arrested a suspected ammunition supplier and recovered 300 rounds of 7.62 x 39mm ammunition concealed in a sack of beans in Kogi State. The operation took place at about 9:30 pm on Tuesday, 17 November 2026. Acting on credible intelligence, soldiers of the Atsawa Blocking Force, working with local vigilantes, intercepted 47-year-old Umaru Muhammad, a resident of Ashe Village. A thorough search revealed the ammunition carefully hidden inside the sack of beans. Security operatives also recovered a Bajaj motorcycle, a mobile phone and the sum of ₦30,500 from the suspect. Umaru Muhammad is currently in military custody as investigators work to uncover the full extent of the suspected supply network and identify other persons who may be linked to the illicit transaction. In a statement issued on Wednesday, the Acting Director of Army Public Relations, Colonel Appolonia Anele, said “the successful interception forms part of the Army’s sustained efforts to disrupt the logistics and ammunition supply chains that support banditry and other criminal activities.” The army urged members of the public to remain vigilant and promptly report any suspicious movement of concealed arms, ammunition or other prohibited items to the nearest security agency.
